draft.text: You came in because you have had sharp, shooting pain on the outside of your right elbow for three weeks.
The pain gets worse when you use your arm, grip things, lift things, or straighten your arm.
The pain is near the bony part of your elbow called the lateral epicondyle.
There is no swelling, redness, or warmth around the area.
You have no history of injury or surgery on your right elbow.
You play tennis more now, which may be related to the pain.
You are willing to have a physical exam and imaging tests like an X-ray or MRI to check the cause of your pain.
